title: Rabbi Naftali Besser: Staying Inspired- "Parashat Bereshit"

chapters.title: Divine Names in Beresheet and Rashi's Explanation
Generating Mercy and the Destruction of the Mabul
The Ramban on the World's Balance and Chesed
Noah's Legacy and Faith in the Teiva

claims: "He discusses the severity of robbery and geneivat da'at, and examines the actions and beliefs of Noah and Avraham." - The transcript does not contain a discussion of Avraham's beliefs or actions in the context of the class, other than a brief mention of his marriage.
summary: Rabbi Besser explores the concept of divine judgment versus mercy in Beresheet, explaining how acts of chesed and interpersonal behavior impact the world's survival. He discusses the severity of robbery and geneivat da'at, and examines the actions and beliefs of Noah and Avraham.
questions: Why does the Torah use different names for God in chapter one and chapter two of Beresheet?
How does human kindness or lack of it affect the entire world?
Why was the generation of the flood punished specifically with destruction over robbery?
What is the halakhic definition and scope of geneivat da'at?
What are the differing views on Noah's righteousness and level of faith?
